content.comment_body: Hello, I'm setting up home lighting and blinds control using [company_name] modules (24V). I just purchased several base modules and digital extension modules. For each base module, I created a diagram using [product_name] engineering software; each diagram handles specific functions: lighting control for different floors and blinds control, including automated operation with sensors. I've integrated these into a network project within the engineering software, with some network links between the devices. My first question: if I modify something in the network project, will those changes automatically update the original diagrams—or are they just static copies once imported? I created these FBD diagrams on a MacBook Air, which doesn’t have Ethernet. What’s the best way to transfer the network program to the modules? I planned to use a microSD card, but now I only have one network file—should I copy this into all base modules, or will the engineering software automatically assign the correct diagrams as configured? How do I interconnect all three devices—should I connect each one to my router or use WiFi for direct communication? Also, is the following IP address setup correct: 192.168.0.1, 192.168.0.2, 192.168.0.3 for the modules, and 192.168.0.233 for the PC, all with the subnet mask 255.255.255.0? Thanks!

Regarding network addressing: instead of using 1, 2, and 3 for device IPs, I recommend using higher numbers, such as 11, 12, and 13. If you are unable to transfer programs over the network and need to use a microSD card, you must export each diagram from the network project separately. Click on the respective module in the network view and select export; this will save each diagram as an individual file. Then, open each file with the engineering software, and save as binary files onto the correct microSD card for each unit. The devices can be integrated into your home network by LAN cable or WiFi, but since the modules do not have built-in WiFi, you will need a WiFi receiver with a LAN output.

Thank you for your prompt reply. Could you confirm that the following setup is valid: PC connected via WiFi, base modules 1, 2, and 3 connected to the router via Ethernet cable (and thanks for the suggestion on using different IP addresses)? Is it possible to upload the network program from my PC (using the engineering software) via WiFi to the modules? Thanks!
Yes, this setup is possible. Just make sure to select the correct network interface card in the transfer settings.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are deploying a multi-device home automation solution using [company_name] base modules and digital extension modules, managed via [product_name] engineering software on a MacBook Air. Key challenges include clarifying whether network edits propagate to individual diagrams, exporting and distributing diagrams effectively, and connecting devices without Ethernet ports. There is uncertainty regarding distributing network diagrams per device and integrating modules into a wired or WiFi network for inter-device communication.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy method to assign network diagrams to individual modules and seamless hardware integration for program uploading, whether via WiFi or LAN—even when using devices without native Ethernet support.
